title: Anchorless warmup experiments and observability journal
content:
Purpose: This notebook captures a set of experiments and operational guidance for an alternative warmup methodology we call "anchorless warmup". The goal: achieve repeatable steady-state throughput without relying on fixed occupancy anchors (steady client counts) that mask cross-run variability. This doc is a running lab journal — contains hypotheses, telemetry charts to collect, run checklist, and a lightweight run template for the bench harness.

Background and motivation:
- Problem: our historical anchoring approach (pick an occupancy target X and drive until token/sec stabilizes) is brittle for heterogeneous clusters and for models with non-linear cold-to-hot transitions. Small differences in client start time, RNG seeds, or GC pauses change priming behavior and cause +/-10-30% spread in throughput claims.
- Anchorless idea: instead of pinning to a single occupancy, use a telemetry-driven priming phase with a small set of probe/spectator clients that drive observability signals (GPU SM util, L2 read/write, CPU steal, KV cache hit-rate) and let the harness progress into steady-state once signal convergence thresholds are met. This reduces dependence on client count exactness and surfaces hardware-induced variance.

Key telemetry signals to collect (minimum):
- per-GPU SM utilization (5s window)
- GPU memory bandwidth utilization (p95)
- Kernel execution tail-latency (99th token generation time)
- KV cache hit-rate and cache fill rate
- Inference queue depth and mean batch size observed in runtime
- OS-level CPU steal, load-average, and per-client tail latency
- Process-level GC/compaction events (if applicable)
- Harness-level request RTT and success/failure rate

Signal heuristics and convergence rules (operational):
- Warmup phase exits when all of the following hold for 3 consecutive 30s windows:
  - median SM util within +/-5% of the 5-minute running median
  - KV cache hit-rate change < 2 percentage points
  - mean batch size observed change < 0.1 tokens per inference
  - 99th-token latency shows monotonic decline plateau (<5% change across windows)
- If any hardware counter shows abrupt jumps (GPU throttling, ECC events), abort and mark the run as contaminated.

Probe client design and placement:
- Probe clients (3 per GPU-pool by default) issue a small randomized set of requests designed to exercise sequence-length and prefix patterns we expect in production. They are lightweight and independent of main load clients.
- Spectator clients are instrumented to collect internal runtime stats and export them to the bench telemetry pipeline (Prometheus pushgateway / bench ingest).
- Probes intentionally include cold prefixes occasionally to surface cache fill rates. Frequency: 1 cold-ish probe per 60s per probe-client.

Load gen configuration recommendations:
- Use gradual phase-based ramp: 0->10% target QPS in 30s, 10->50% in 90s, 50->target in 180s. These are starting heuristics; the warmup phase above supersedes fixed timers.
- Interleave jittered inter-arrival times using a truncated-normal distribution instead of pure poisson to reduce burst edge effects that confound kernel selection heuristics. Std dev = 0.25*mean; clip at 0.1*mean and 2.5*mean.
- Set per-client RNG seeds deterministically for the client population per run (record them) to allow replay, but allow controlled entropy injection in probe clients to surface cache behaviors.
- Tokenization: ensure the token length distribution matches production percentiles (p50, p90, p99) — we include a tiny sample-scorer that computes drift against production histograms prior to the run.

Reproducibility practices and run hygiene:
- Record and store: git commit of harness, CLI args, full set of client seeds, model binary hash, driver/kernel versions, and all telemetry snapshots. If any low-level driver version differs by patch, mark runs as non-comparable.
- Always run at least 3 full trials (same config/seeds) per cell. Compute median-run as canonical; report p10/p90 spread.
- Use a stable-run filter: discard runs that trigger hardware interrupts, ECC or GPU reset events. Maintain a list of reasons for discards.

Anchoring-free bake-in experiments we ran (summary):
- EXP-A (2024-11-12): small 2xA100 box, n=3 probe clients, target occupancy 128 tokens/GPU. Anchorless converged after 4.5 minutes; spread across 5 trials = 4.2% p90/p10.
- EXP-B (2024-12-03): heterogeneous fleet (A100+H100 mix), observed that SM util plateaus diverged per device type; we added device-specific probe clients and device-weighted convergence rules — reduced cross-device spread from 18% -> 7%.
- EXP-C (2025-01-21): quantized 4-bit path; found that kernel fallback due to tiny sequence-length jitter caused batch-size swings. We mitigated by enabling small batch padding in the runtime (pad to nearest multiple of 8 tokens for micro-batching). Repeatability improved but average throughput dropped 3% (tradeoff).

Troubleshooting checklist (if warmup never converges):
- Check for background noise: run nvidia-smi top and host top. Any other processes?
- Verify power cap and thermal events: throttling can take minutes to normalize.
- Inspect client clocks: >200ms skew on clients can perturb inter-arrival patterns and break convergence heuristics.
- If KV cache hit-rate oscillates, replay probe-only trace to measure cache steady-state time independent of main load.

Run template (copy-paste friendly):
1) Git snapshot: git rev-parse HEAD -> record
2) Prepare harness config: 
   - model: model-v3-quant
   - target-occupancy-hint: 0.6 (hint only)
   - client-count: 96
   - probe-clients: 3 per pool
   - seed-file: /bench/seeds/2025-01-21-seedset.json
3) Start bench telemetry: bench-telemetry start --dest prometheus:9091
4) Start runtime with logging level INFO and telemetry hooks enabled
5) Kick off run: bench-run --config bench-config.yaml --watch-probes
6) Wait for convergence signal (bench-run will emit "WARMUP: CONVERGED") or fail with contamination
7) Run steady-state measurement window 10m after convergence, then stop clients and capture final snapshot

Metrics to report in run artifact (minimum):
- steady-state token/s (median across clients), p90/p10
- mean batch size and batch-size distribution
- KV cache hit-rate at start and steady-state
- 99th-token latency during steady-state
- telemetry convergence time (seconds) and number of re-tries/aborts

Notes on interpretation and claims:
- Because anchorless is telemetry-driven, always include the convergence triggers and telemetry traces when publishing throughput claims. Consumers must be able to re-evaluate claims by re-running the same seeds against the same runtime and telemetry convergence rules.
- Anchorless runs are intentionally conservative: we favor a robust plateau rather than the single highest instantaneous throughput sample.

Open questions / future work:
- Can we learn optimal probe patterns automatically per model via a small meta-benchmark? (train a model that predicts convergence time given probe mix)
- How does anchorless interact with multi-tenant noise? We need experiments with background synthetic tenants to measure false convergence risks.
- Can we extend the convergence rule set with machine-learned anomaly detectors to reduce manual thresholds?

Appendix: quick diagnostics commands
- probe-only replay: bench-run --replay probes.json --no-main-load --collect-telemetry
- export run artifact: bench-artifact export --run-id 2025-01-21-anchless-expC --out s3://bench-artifacts/

Action items:
- [ ] Add anchorless mode toggle to bench-run CLI and persist convergence rule overrides in config file (Ben)
- [ ] Add device-level probe placement automation (Liang)
- [ ] Draft a short tech note comparing anchor-based vs anchorless best-practices for the public benchmarking page (Maya)

If you run this and see a recurrence of >10% spread across trials, collect the full telemetry bundle and ping #eng-serving-runtime with the run id and attached artifact.

End of journal entry.
